$comment: THE CONTRACT BETWEEN TWO REPOSITORY HALVES THAT NEVER IMPORT EACH OTHER.
The identity service carries the MemQL editor as a compiled-in first-party OAuth
client (component/identity/builtin_clients.go). The VS Code extension authorizes as
that client without registering (editors/vscode/src/auth/wellKnownClient.ts). Nothing
in the build links the two: they are separate languages, separate modules and separate
release artifacts, and each is individually tested.
So the two constants below have to be written down once and asserted from both sides.
A disagreement is invisible until a released extension meets a released cluster, and it
presents as 'Unknown client' on the consent page or as invalid_client on /device/code --
which reads exactly like the 403 registration_disabled failure this work removed, and
would send the next reader down the same wrong path (memql#4514).
'redirectURI' is PORTLESS and that is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. The extension's
loopback listener takes an ephemeral port, so the URI the browser actually returns to
carries a different number every sign-in. RFC 8252 section 7.3 grants an any-port
exception ONLY to a registered loopback URI with no explicit port -- a registered URI
that carries a port opts back into exact-match (component/identity/config.go,
matchesLoopbackAnyPort). Adding a port here would silently break every callback.
Read by component/identity/first_party_client_contract_test.go (Go) and
editors/vscode/test/firstPartyClientContract.test.ts (TypeScript). Changing a value
here obliges both -- and strands every already-released editor, so treat it as frozen.
